english.title: Arrest by constable - surety notifying desire to withdraw from acting as such
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) you were arrested by a constable, being a person released on **(..SPECIFY DATE BAILED..) by

(A)_[**(..SPECIFY COURT..)]_
(B)_[the custody officer at **(..SPECIFY POLICE STATION..)]_

with a surety in the sum of **(..SPECIFY THE AMOUNT..) provided by **(..SPECIFY THE NAME OF THE PERSON PROVIDING THE SURETY..),

(C)_[he]_
(D)_[she]_

having now informed

(E)_[the Court]_
(F)_[a police officer]_

that they now no longer wish to act in that capacity
english.legislation: Contrary to section 7(3)(c), (4) and (5) of the Bail Act 1976.

english.notes:
The above 'wording' is NOT AN OFFENCE.

(i) This wording is supplied by P.N.L.D. for information only (some forces do prepare a 'charge form' for administrative purposes i.e. to generate an entry on the court register, to assist the court).
(ii) IMPORTANT: A person arrested for breach of bail conditions under section 7(3) MUST physically appear before a magistrate's court WITHIN TWENTY FOUR HOURS of his arrest - this is an ABSOLUTE REQUIREMENT. His mere presence within the precincts of the court within that time period will not suffice. (R v Governor of Glen Parva Young Offenders Institution, Ex Parte G 1998 - The Times 24.1.98). It is also vital to realise that unless the defendant is arrested within 24 hours of his forthcoming court hearing, he must go before a magistrates, and NOT returned to the Court from which he was originally bailed.

NOTE:
(i) The requirement to appear before a court "IN THE PETTY SESSIONAL AREA WHERE HE WAS ARRESTED" was repealed by paragraph 185 of Schedule 8 to the Courts Act 2003, effectively therefore, there is no requirement to bring a bail breacher before the court in the area where he was arrested, BUT, officers should think very carefully before bringing a person before a court other than one local to the area in which the arrest took place
(ii) The above situation commonly arises with absconders from bail hostels. They are frequently arrested hundreds of miles from the scene of their original crime. An escort should not be sent to fetch them (outside the 24 hour limit) but every assistance should, of course, be given to the arresting force so that the necessary information can be put before the Court in that area.

(iii) In reckoning any period of twenty four hours for the above purpose no account shall be taken of Christmas Day, Good Friday or any Sunday.
(iv) This procedure can be used where an individual has breached a custody officer's bail conditions as well as court conditions.
(v) See H575 where the offender has simply failed to answer his bail and H567 where the offender had a reasonable excuse for not answering his bail and then failed to surrender as soon as practicable.
(vi) While local force procedure should always be complied with, as a general guide it is felt that in order to deal with the above circumstances a court file should include where necessary some or all of the following:- front sheet, check list; defendant details; summary; confidential information; copy of initial remand form; opposition to bail and copies of any statement(s) in support of the breach

other.powersofarrest: Section 7(3) of the Bail Act provides a power of arrest for a constable who has reasonable grounds for suspecting that a person has broken any of his bail conditions.
other.timelimitforprosecutions: Not applicable - this is NOT AN OFFENCE
other.penalty:
Not applicable - this is NOT AN OFFENCE

In spite of the fact that a power of arrest exists for breaching bail conditions it is NOT an offence. Procedures whereby the case is presented at court will vary from force to force, however, some magistrates clerks demand some form of paper work to be completed which generates an entry in the court register. Therefore to assist forces who require this procedure the above 'pseudo' standard offence wording is provided.

A court may however impose sterner conditions on the offender or remand in custody.
